Class RemoteMethodsImplementation

java.lang.Object
java.rmi.server.RemoteObject
java.rmi.server.RemoteServer
java.rmi.server.UnicastRemoteObject
it.polimi.ingsw.mesos.RMI.RemoteMethodsImplementation
All Implemented Interfaces:
RemoteMethods, Serializable, Remote
public class RemoteMethodsImplementation extends UnicastRemoteObject implements RemoteMethods
Implementation of the RemoteMethods interface. This class represents the server-side entry point for all RMI client requests. It receives remote invocations from clients and delegates the execution of game and lobby actions to the ServerState and GameController components. All game-related actions are executed asynchronously using an ExecutorService to avoid blocking the RMI thread pool and to ensure better scalability.

    • heartbeat

      public void heartbeat(String nickname) throws RemoteException
      Records the current timestamp for the given player as proof of an active connection.

      This method is called periodically by the client-side KeepAliveRMI at a fixed interval. Each invocation updates the player's entry in lastHeartbeat with the current system time, resetting the inactivity countdown monitored by the watchdog thread started in startWatchdog().

      Specified by:
      heartbeat in interface RemoteMethods
      Parameters:
      nickname - name of the player sending the heartbeat, used as the key to update the timestamp map
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if a network error occurs during the remote call

    • startWatchdog

      private void startWatchdog()
      Starts a background watchdog thread that periodically checks all connected players for heartbeat timeouts and handles disconnections accordingly.

      The watchdog runs on a single-threaded scheduled executor and fires every 5 seconds. On each tick it iterates over the lastHeartbeat map and compares the current system time against each player's last recorded heartbeat. If the elapsed time exceeds 50 seconds, the player is considered disconnected and the following cleanup sequence is triggered:

      1. The player's entry is removed from lastHeartbeat.
      2. A timeout message is printed to stdout for diagnostics.
      3. GameController.onPlayerDisconnected(String) is called on the player's active game controller (if present), so the game logic can react to the disconnection (e.g. pausing the game or reassigning the turn).
      4. ServerState.removePlayer(String) is called to clean up all remaining server-side references to the player.
